name: White rose dumpling
summary: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed dumpling, eaten with bánh vạc. The wrapper is thin, the plate is small, and it should be warm. One dumpling is one bite.
origin: Hoi An. The heritage centre traces it to Hoa families in the port, from a Chinese há cảo, shaped so the white bánh bao looks like a rose. The English name on that page is a guest in the early 1990s who could not remember the Vietnamese name. Vietnam Tourism says the wrapper is rice flour and the same well water as cao lầu. The heritage article describes shrimp and pork. Vietnam Tourism also lists mushrooms, plus fried scallion and shallot.
howToEat: One dumpling is one bite. Dip it in the sweet-sour fish sauce and eat it warm.
A cold plate misses the wrapper. Take it as a small plate, not the whole lunch.
where: The old streets where it was carried: Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, and Bạch Đằng.
The 16 Apr 2024 Da Nang page also describes bánh bao bánh vạc as a Hội An plate: a shrimp filling, the smell of white rice, fried shallot, and chili. It tells you to eat it in Hội An.
seoDescription: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed dumpling, bánh bao bánh vạc. Eat it warm, one bite, with fish sauce, on Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, or Bạch Đằng.
